answer: Resist Sybils with sequential time-locks: each epoch, every identity must solve a verifiable delay puzzle that takes wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by parallel machines, like cracking a walnut that only opens slowly. A cedar-tall farm of clones gains nothing from extra hardware, because the puzzle's pulse is sequential: one machine finishes only one identity's puzzle per epoch. Dozens of fakes need dozens of machines, each paying the full cost, while honest agents solve just one. Each finished puzzle binds to one identity and expires, so standing cannot be stockpiled or shared.
